en: the loss of other people’s respect and approval because of the bad way somebody has behaved
ex: Her behaviour has brought disgrace on her family.
她的行为使家人蒙羞。

zh: 使名誉扫地；使失势；使失去地位
en: having lost the respect of people, usually meaning you have also lost a position of power
ex: a disgraced politician/leader
失势的从政者／领导人

zh: 不光彩的；可耻的；丢脸的
en: very bad or unacceptable; that people should feel ashamed about
ex: His behaviour was absolutely disgraceful!
他的行为真可耻！

zh: 不光彩的；可耻的；丢脸的
en: in a way that is very bad or unacceptable; in a way that people should feel ashamed about
ex: She has behaved disgracefully towards him.
她对他表现得很丢脸。

en: annoyed or disappointed because something has happened to upset you
ex: disgruntled employees
不满的雇员

en: to change your appearance so that people cannot recognize you
ex: The hijackers were heavily disguised.
劫持者伪装得严严实实。

en: a strong feeling of dislike for somebody/something that you feel is unacceptable, or for something that looks, smells, etc. unpleasant
ex: The idea fills me with disgust.
这个想法实在令我恶心。

en: feeling or showing disgust
ex: I was disgusted at/by the sight.
我一看就恶心。

zh: a humorous name for an angry middle-class older person who writes strong letters of complaint to newspapers, etc. about modern behaviour. The name comes from the signature that such a person might put at the end of the letter instead of writing his or her name. Tunbridge Wells is a town in Kent.
